bull_case: Nu sustains high-teens/20%+ growth with 30%+ ROE, Mexico and Colombia scale toward Brazil-like economics, and data/AI improves underwriting enough to support materially higher distributable earnings per share.
bear_case: Credit growth outruns underwriting, NPL/ECL and funding costs rise, Brazil matures faster than expected, and required capital retention prevents reported earnings growth from becoming distributable owner earnings.
thesis: At $14.03, NU trades at about 0.756x the locked Base value of $18.56. Q2 2026 delivered $1.06B net income and 33% ROE while customers reached 139M, but banking cash cannot be treated as excess cash. The key valuation issue is how much earnings can be distributed after retaining capital for 20%+ growth. Current price allows Base execution with a meaningful, not extreme, margin of safety.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 accounting revenue was $5.513B and net income $1.061B; managerial ROE was 33%.
Q2 customers reached 138.9M, ARPAC $17.1, and managerial revenue $5.876B; revenue grew 39% YoY on an FX-neutral basis.
The Q2 credit portfolio was $39.4B, up 37% YoY, while 15-90 NPL improved to 4.8% and 90+ NPL rose to 6.9%.
Q2 total equity was $13.252B and diluted weighted-average shares were 4.904837B; NU also repurchased $500.4M of shares in H1.
Using the locked 9%/10-year policy and a bank-specific distributable owner-earnings/share proxy, Bear/Base/Bull values are about $4.76/$18.56/$34.85; price/Base is 0.7558x.
evidence.source: Harness locked owner-FCF/share DCF using bank-specific distributable owner-earnings proxy

counterevidence: The valuation proxy is structurally less direct than industrial FCF because distributable earnings depend on capital requirements and local regulatory buffers.
Q2 90+ NPL rose to 6.9% as the portfolio intentionally moved into higher-risk/higher-return segments.
Brazil remains the dominant exposure, so BRL, rates and regulation materially affect USD shareholder outcomes.
The $1B repurchase authorization improves per-share economics only if shares are bought below intrinsic value and capital remains comfortably above requirements.
unknowns: Long-run target capital ratios and excess capital available for distribution by geography.
Normalized loss rates as unsecured and higher-risk cohorts season.
Sustainable ROE after Mexico/Colombia reach larger scale and Brazil matures.
A reproducible five-year valuation percentile for a bank-appropriate metric.
falsifiers: ROE falls structurally below the mid-20s while revenue growth remains capital intensive.
90+ NPL/ECL rises persistently enough to compress risk-adjusted NIM and capital generation.
Mexico/Colombia require substantially more capital than assumed without converging toward attractive unit economics.
